items.title: Reflexio
items.name: Reflexio
items.summary: Behavioral learning that makes AI agents better over time
items.description: Reflexio makes AI agents better with every interaction. When users correct an agent, a path fails, or something works particularly well, Reflexio turns that experience into behavior the agent can reuse next time. Instead of leaving valuable lessons buried in logs, your agent continuously learns what to repeat and what to avoid — with every learning visible, testable, and reversible. Reduce task failure rate by more than 30%, while saving tokens by more than 60%.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt 👋
I'm Yi, co-founder of Reflexio. Before starting Reflexio, I was tech lead in Meta and adjunct professor at University of Washington teaching ML and business applications.

Today we're launching Reflexio: a learning platform that makes your AI agents fail less and burn fewer tokens, by learning from what actually happens in production.

Here's what got us started: people use AI agents every day, but agents never actually get better with use. Even with memory, an agent that failed a task yesterday will fail the same way today, across different users — because nothing connects what happened in production back to how the agent behaves next time. The online learning loop just isn't there.

We learned firsthand that closing that loop manually — reading traces, spotting failures, rewriting prompts — is a painful, never-ending job.
Reflexio autonomously observes your agent's live traces, learns from successes, failures, and user corrections, and continuously optimizes behavior. No manual tuning.

The results? In our case studies, agents with Reflexio:

  • 🎯 Cut task failure rate by 36%

  • 💸 Reduced token usage by 57%

  • 📈 Improved response quality in 47% of interactions, with negligible regressions

Try it today: sign up free at reflexio.ai and get 30 days of Pro on us.

Congrats on the launch. The 30% failure drop and 60% token savings numbers are strong, how did you actually measure those? Was it an A/B between agents with and without Reflexio on the same task set, or before/after on the same production traffic?

interesting approach - the generalized-rule part is what gives me pause though. if one user's "correction" is actually bad advice (they misunderstood the task, or just pushed the agent toward a wrong answer confidently), and that gets rolled up into a rule applied to every user, how do you catch that before it spreads? is there some confidence threshold or does every generalized rule need a human to sign off before it goes from "one user's pattern" to "everyone's default behavior"?

items.title: Routines by Databox
items.name: Routines by Databox
items.summary: An AI Analyst that runs analysis and reports on a schedule
items.description: Give your AI Analyst a prompt and a schedule. It analyzes your live data, prepares the report or analysis you asked for, and delivers it by email, Slack, or in-app. The recurring work you do by hand today gets done automatically.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I'm Pete from Databox. Excited to finally share Routines with you.

This is the next capability launch in our agentic analytics platform. The first one, our AI Analyst Genie, made analysis instant. Ask a question about your live data, and you get a finished answer in minutes. The second, Artifacts, turned those answers into polished, shareable reports. But both still begin the same way, with a person opening a chat and asking.

So we built Routines.

Routines let you put recurring analysis on a schedule. Give our AI Analyst a prompt and a cadence, and it runs the analysis and delivers the finished report on its own, every time it's due:

  • Your recurring analysis runs itself: every run happens on schedule, without anyone remembering to start it. (It can also be triggered by a webhook from another system.)

  • You can act from the notification alone: each run arrives by email, Slack, or in-app with a summary that tells you how things stand.

  • Every answer stays available: runs are saved in the routine, so you can revisit any report or continue the conversation with a follow-up question

  • Your own analysis becomes repeatable: save the way you analyze something as a Skill once, then put it on a schedule

All of that is what makes Routines a critical part of our agentic analytics platform.

Without agentic analytics, analysis must be done by a person. Routines delivers it to people instead.

In the old way, someone pulls the numbers, figures out what moved and why, writes it up, and sends it around. The team talks about it a few days later. The next round happens when that skilled person has time for it again, usually a week or a month out. So analysis happens as often as one person's calendar allows, only the people on that email ever see it, and anything that goes wrong in between doesn't get caught.

With analysis done on a schedule using Routines, a Tuesday problem gets flagged on Tuesday and the plan changes that week instead of next month.

And anyone can be on the delivery list, including people one function over, so the teams that support each other work from the same explanation at the same time. For example, with the right Routine setup, marketing can see that sales is converting leads at a lower rate than last month and can dig into lead quality or push volume up before anyone raises it in a meeting.

We've been testing it internally for weeks. Our team members are more informed, and we spend meetings deciding what to do instead of reviewing what happened.

Routines is live today. Try it out on your account, or start a trial: https://help.databox.com/start-a-trial

If there's a report you'd like to fully automate, tell us about it below. We'll set it up for the first five people who ask, no charge for our time.
Having every routine run stay searchable later so you're not digging thru chat for last week's check is a really nice touch. Looking forward to what you build next!

This is probably the launch I’m most proud of recently -> our first agentic notification layer that actually feels useful.

I was getting bored of, and mostly ignoring, repetitive emails like “XY has been delivered, click here to see more.”


With Routines, the agentic analysis happens in the background, and the notification gives you just enough context to understand what’s happening and get a sense of how your day or week is going.

And if you want to understand something in more detail, you’re just one click away from a deeper analysis and more insights. GJ team!

idea_items.title: AI 应用场景 / 数据
idea_items.need_line: B端产品经理在梳理业务全场景时，最耗神的是要把角色、单据、业务流程、数据传递等要素完整拆出并落到需求文档，手工做慢且担心遗漏。
idea_items.status_line: 当下讨论集中在用流程模板和个人方法论来兜底，很多人按标准产品/定制产品分类，再通过梳理组织架构、分角色访谈和整理业务流程来产出需求。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪把角色-单据-流程-数据传递等梳理结构做成的半自动场景建模辅助，让产品经理以结构化输入快速生成全场景需求清单。
tags: AI 应用场景 / 数据

idea_items.title: 教育 AI 辅导
idea_items.need_line: 教师备课时需要同时处理资料理解、课件制作、教案编写等任务，在多个工具和资源平台间切换导致效率低下。
idea_items.status_line: 当前讨论集中在用AI单点工具分别处理：用文档阅读总结工具快速吃透资料、用PPT生成工具做课件、用对话式AI写教案，再搭配各省教育资源平台和模板网站找现成课件。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪的方向是面向备课任务链的“输入资料即出全套教案+课件框架”的AI助手，让教师不需要在多个工具和资源站之间来回切换，重点是把现有单点能力整合进教师自己的课件与教材语料里。

idea_items.title: 法律 AI 工作流
idea_items.need_line: 用户在缺少完整交易背景的情况下，需要快速判断一份合同能否签字以及有哪些关键风险。
idea_items.status_line: 律师强调必须与客户确认交易模式和背景后才能实质审查，而普通用户常直接甩来合同或套用模板，双方在半小时完成“要不要签字”的预期与实际数天工作量之间存在明显落差。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪的方向是把交易背景问答与合同条款风险提示结合起来，让 AI 先补齐背景再给出签字建议，而不是只做文本逐条校对。

interest_sections.title: AI 面试官
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是AI面试辅助正从诚信陪练滑向实时作弊工具，而真正的缺口在面试官侧对AI作答的识别能力。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 候选人需要针对目标岗位生成贴合自身项目经历的模拟面试问答和讲稿，而不是照念AI实时生成的通用答案

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 目前有两类做法：一类是实时监听面试问题、让AI生成答案并照着念的作弊类App；另一类是用GitHub项目如job-hunt-copilot建立项目素材库，再自动生成定制简历和面试讲稿用于模拟面试。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是反作弊侧的AI面试检测机制，从读稿停顿感、回答与简历矛盾点、突然断线等行为信号实时识别AI辅助作答并反馈给面试官。

items.paragraph: B端产品经理在梳理业务全场景时，最耗神的是要把角色、单据、业务流程、数据传递等要素完整拆出并落到需求文档，手工做慢且担心遗漏

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当下讨论集中在用流程模板和个人方法论来兜底，很多人按标准产品/定制产品分类，再通过梳理组织架构、分角色访谈和整理业务流程来产出需求。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪把角色-单据-流程-数据传递等梳理结构做成的半自动场景建模辅助，让产品经理以结构化输入快速生成全场景需求清单。

interest_sections.title: 教育 AI 辅导
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，显示新手教师备课仍是被文档处理、课件制作、教案撰写三个环节拆散，需求方向是让AI按‘材料理解-教学设计-课件生成’顺序自动流转。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前讨论集中在用AI单点工具分别处理：用文档阅读总结工具快速吃透资料、用PPT生成工具做课件、用对话式AI写教案，再搭配各省教育资源平台和模板网站找现成课件。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是面向备课任务链的“输入资料即出全套教案+课件框架”的AI助手，让教师不需要在多个工具和资源站之间来回切换，重点是把现有单点能力整合进教师自己的课件与教材语料里。

interest_sections.title: 法律 AI 工作流
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub；合同审查的耗时不止在读条款，更在缺少交易背景，AI 的机会在于把背景询问和风险研判嵌入审查流程，并降低非专业人士自行套用模板的隐患。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 用户在缺少完整交易背景的情况下，需要快速判断一份合同能否签字以及有哪些关键风险

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 律师强调必须与客户确认交易模式和背景后才能实质审查，而普通用户常直接甩来合同或套用模板，双方在半小时完成“要不要签字”的预期与实际数天工作量之间存在明显落差。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是把交易背景问答与合同条款风险提示结合起来，让 AI 先补齐背景再给出签字建议，而不是只做文本逐条校对。

interest_sections.title: AI 面试官
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是AI面试辅助正从诚信陪练滑向实时作弊工具，而真正的缺口在面试官侧对AI作答的识别能力。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 候选人需要针对目标岗位生成贴合自身项目经历的模拟面试问答和讲稿，而不是照念AI实时生成的通用答案

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 目前有两类做法：一类是实时监听面试问题、让AI生成答案并照着念的作弊类App；另一类是用GitHub项目如job-hunt-copilot建立项目素材库，再自动生成定制简历和面试讲稿用于模拟面试。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是反作弊侧的AI面试检测机制，从读稿停顿感、回答与简历矛盾点、突然断线等行为信号实时识别AI辅助作答并反馈给面试官。
